bib.title: From Trainee to Trainer: LLM-Designed Training Environment for RL with Multi-Agent Reasoning

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "From Trainee to Trainer: LLM-Designed Training Environment for RL with Multi-Agent Reasoning". First author Chao Chen (LARK, HKUST-GZ), with Chengzu Li, Zhiwei Li, Yinhong Liu, Zhijiang Guo. arXiv:2606.17682v1 [cs.CL], 16 Jun 2026. Preprint, no venue. Code and weights are on GitHub and HF (LARK-AI-Lab).
COVERAGE: 18 of 18 pages, 48,091 of 48,091 chars, including the appendices (A validity checks, B per-variant results, C hyperparameters, D prompts, E limitations). References were skimmed. Figures were not rendered. I used only the text extraction.

CLAIMS (ranked)
1. A 4B policy that redesigns its own environment generator beats the frontier LLMs and fixed-config GRPO on aggregate valid/optimal rate.
 - number: 3-agent Sum 51.67 valid / 31.67 optimal. 4-agent 33.14 / 21.33. 5-agent 18.67 / 11.00. Kimi-K2.5 (best baseline): 46.17/29.25, 26.95/17.90, 13.47/8.78. GRPO(random): 40.42/26.08, 26.67/16.10, 15.11/9.11. Base Qwen3-4B: 14.83/14.00, 3.43/3.05, 1.44/1.22.
 - setup: Qwen3-4B, GRPO in verl. Trained only on 2-agent instances, 3x3 to 10x10, 4000 instances per round, 3 rounds. Evaluated on 3/4/5-agent MAPF-FrozenLake (50 samples per map size per wait-ratio subset). Baselines: GPT-5.4, Grok-4.2, Gemini-3.1-Pro, Kimi-K2.5. "Sum" appears to be the mean over sizes, not a sum.
 - quote: "our framework improves the valid rate by +5.20 to +6.19 points and the optimal rate by +2.22 to +3.43 points." (p.8). Also: "adds +3.56 to +11.25 points of valid rate and +1.89 to +5.59 points of optimal rate" over GRPO (random) (p.8).
 - where: Tables 2-4, p.7-8.
2. The current RL checkpoint is a better environment engineer than the untrained base model.
 - number: valid/optimal 51.67/31.67 vs 45.21/30.00 (3-agent). 33.14/21.33 vs 27.62/19.62 (4-agent). 18.67/11.00 vs 16.00/10.89 (5-agent).
 - setup: same framework, only the engineer model swapped. The base engineer starves 7x7-10x10 in R1 and gives each only about 9% in R2.
 - quote: "policy learning sharpens the model's ability to diagnose its own remaining weaknesses" (p.11). Table 8, p.12.
3. Ablation on training details (T): bookkeeping only beats full RL details.
 - number: full RL details 38.83/26.50, 24.76/18.19, 14.22/10.11 vs bookkeeping 51.67/31.67, 33.14/21.33, 18.67/11.00 (3/4/5-agent).
 - quote: "the model mainly needs to know where it is in the training loop, while detailed RL parameters can distract it from the current failure evidence." (p.11)
 - Caveat: the "Ours" row is called V6 and also "bookkeeping only". The text says V6 includes the training-details module, so the label is ambiguous.
4. Context-module ablation, six variants V1-V6 (failure breakdown F, guideline, history with/without round-0 default, self-summary, training details). The ranking on valid rate, aggregated over 3/4/5-agent, runs V6 > V4 > V3 > V2 > V5 > V1.
 - number: Fig 8 valid rates for wr_025/050/075 are V1 25.2/18.4/14.9, V2 36.6/26.9/19.7, V3 38.8/31.0/23.9, V4 41.4/33.6/25.2, V5 32.6/24.6/19.7, V6 45.2/35.7/27.3. The assignment of the six-number rows to variants is my reading of the figure text.
 - Findings: V5's self-summary overrides the raw failure data and hurts. Removing the round-0 default helps (V4 > V3). Full rewrites degrade healthy sizes. V6 down-weights the hardest 10x10 (data_ratio 0.05 then 0.03) and shifts budget to 7x7.
 - quote: "The context should provide facts as much as possible, rather than only interpretations of those facts." (p.10)
 - where: Table 5, Figs 3-6, Table 6, p.9-10. Fig 8, p.15.
5. Reward design: R = w_acc*R_acc + w_len*R_len.
 - R_acc is 0 if any of 8 validity checks fails. Otherwise it is shaped by cost gap, from 1.0 down to 0.3 at a gap of 2*gt_cost. It falls back to 0.5 if gt_cost can't be parsed.
 - R_len is 0 up to 1500 tokens, falling linearly to -1 at 4096.
 - Weights go from (0.5, 0.5) to (0.8, 0.2) as an EMA of the short-response ratio rises from 0.5 to 0.9.
 - where: Eqs 1-3, p.5. Checks are listed in Appendix A, p.15.
6. Training setup (Appendix C, p.15-16).
 - GRPO, batch 128 prompts x n=8 rollouts, 4xH100, AdamW lr 2e-6, KL beta 1e-3 in the loss, no entropy term, verl v0.6.1, vLLM 0.10.3. Max response length 5120.

Verbatim quotes for the note:
- "the current RL checkpoint serves as a better environment engineer than the original base model" (abstract, p.1)
- "Naively maximizing difficulty is also insufficient: overly difficult environments may collapse the learning signal" (p.2)
- "it represents a single, self-contained task family. The redesign strategies learned by the environment engineer may not directly transfer" (p.18)

LIMITS
- Authors concede: a single task family (MAPF-FrozenLake). No test on other training paradigms. The generator is fixed, so the engineer tunes only data/hole/wait ratios per map size, not mechanics.
- Not shown (my observation):
  - No seeds or variance reported. Each table cell is one run. Per-size n=50, so gaps of a few points are likely within noise.
  - No comparison with a hand-tuned or standard automatic curriculum, despite the intro claiming "carefully-designed curricula". The only fixed baseline is a single random config.
  - The 5-agent gap over GRPO(random) is about 3.6 valid points.
  - The environment-design step is performed by the 4B model itself. No frontier LLM is tested as engineer, despite the abstract's "outperforming larger proprietary LLMs" framing. Those LLMs are compared only as solvers.
  - Only 3 rounds, so R1 and R2 are the only redesigns. The "mechanistic" analysis is qualitative reading of reasoning traces.
  - Validation data and the round-0 config come from the same generator as the training data.
- Internal inconsistency: the main text says "each consisting of two epochs" (p.7), but Appendix C says three RL epochs per round.
- Dating: it cites GPT-5.4, Grok-4.2 and Gemini-3.1-Pro, so the baselines are current for mid-2026.

BUILDS ON: curriculum learning (Bengio 2009; Graves 2017; Florensa 2018; Zhang 2020 value disagreement); LLM curriculum RL (Bae 2026; Xie 2025 Logic-RL; Zeng 2025); self-play and self-improvement (Yuan 2024; Chen 2025 Self-questioning; Huang 2025 R-Zero; Zhou 2026 Self-challenging agents; Liang 2025); AutoEnv (Zhang 2025); the FrozenLake variant from Wu 2025 VSP; Conflict-Based Search for the generator; GRPO via verl.

CODE: none beyond the prompts and the loop. Algorithm 1 (p.5) is: generate D_n = G(C_n); M_{n+1} = GRPO(M_n, D_n; R); validate; compose context; the new model proposes C~_{n+1}; Project() enforces constraints. The prompts are in Appendix D (p.16-18).

FIGURES: Fig 2, p.4: the loop diagram (train, eval, design). Fig 3, p.8: hole/wait ratio vs map size, monotone template vs V6's drop at 10x10. Fig 4: edit-granularity matrix. Fig 6, p.10: self-correction schematic. Fig 7, p.11: data_ratio from base vs RL-checkpoint engineer. Fig 8, p.15: per-variant valid rates.

NOTE FIT (my reading of the note titles; the notes were not opened):
- Note 06 (data and environments): the main fit. It covers LLM-driven environment/curriculum redesign, failure-targeted edits, and the finding that maximizing difficulty is not the goal.
- Note 07 (reward design): the accuracy-times-length adaptive reward with a cost-gap shaped term and the 8 hard validity gates.
- Note 10 (engineering RL systems): the verl/GRPO configuration and the multi-round loop.
- Notes 05 and 08: weak fit. It is a small-scale toy-task result.

PROBLEMS: Table text extraction is run together in places, e.g. "48.0034.00" is 48.00 and 34.00, and "28.00 18.00 ... 10.002.67" is 10.00 and 2.67. Figures were not visually inspected. No embedded instructions were found.
